claims.text: A machine-learning model incorporating electronic-structure descriptors and phase-diagram-derived parameters can predict low phonon thermal conductivity in single-phase CoCrFeMnNi alloys.
The model can achieve prediction error within approximately 15% of experimental values.
The model will outperform conventional empirical rules.
Controlled casting and annealing ensure a homogeneous, single-phase solid-solution microstructure in CoCrFeMnNi.
The relevant single-phase microstructure has significant lattice distortions.
Lattice distortions in the alloy promote phonon scattering.
Valence-electron concentration, lattice-distortion parameters, and phase-diagram contributions are useful descriptors for predicting thermal conductivity.
The machine-learning model captures correlations between electronic structure, lattice distortion, and phonon scattering.
Capturing those correlations allows more accurate thermal-transport predictions than traditional empirical approaches.
Conventional empirical rules and binary-phase-diagram extrapolations typically have larger deviations from experiment than the proposed model.
The claimed predictive accuracy applies to single-phase CoCrFeMnNi alloys processed under controlled conditions.
The model may not apply to multiphase or phase-segregated materials.
Phase segregation introduces additional scattering mechanisms that are not captured by the proposed model.
Model performance is sensitive to the quality and range of the training data.
An independent test-set mean absolute percentage error above 15% is specified as the outcome that falsifies the accuracy hypothesis.
